description: Emulsion Flow Technologies (EFT) advances next-generation separation technologies derived from nuclear science to solve critical global resource and environmental challenges. Enedym is a technology start-up company from McMaster University. The company is headquartered at the McMaster Innovation Park in Hamilton, Ontario, Canada. Enedym’s vision is to significantly reduce the cost of electric motors and electrified powertrains, and power a new paradigm in electrification through novel rare earth metals free electric motors, controls, and digitization techniques. Enedym aspires to help save the planet, one electric motor market at a time.

description: Princeton NuEnergy is a U.S. platform for advanced battery materials manufacturing, delivering cost-effective, capital-efficient production of battery-grade Cathode Active Material (CAM) for lithium-ion batteries. Built on a proprietary, closed-loop system, PNE’s capabilities include Direct Recycling (Cathode-to-Cathode®), Advanced Black Mass™ production, and Upcycled CAM, supporting a stronger domestic battery supply chain and U.S. energy independence.

Reverion develops and builds fuel cell power plants with electrical efficiencies of up to 80%, making them the most efficient in the world. Reverion’s systems are reversible: When electricity prices are high, the units generate power from gas while capturing CO₂. When prices drop, they switch to electrolysis to produce green gases such as hydrogen or methane. By enabling CO₂ storage, they operate CO₂-negative. The power plants of the future, available today.
